description: A no-show recovery drafted for SMS, but only email consent is on record. Option-B (fail-closed) consent BLOCKS the draft — a non-consented channel never proceeds, and no artifact is created. This is the ONE fixture in this suite that REQUIRES a block and can honestly demand it: the consent gate reads `input.channel` against `input.consentedChannels`, both caller-supplied, so the block is determined entirely by the input and cannot depend on the model behaving badly (contrast the three sibling fixtures, whose v1 expectations DID depend on it — see their descriptions). `status` is therefore critical_if_failed: a `succeeded` here means the runtime drafted outbound copy for a channel with no recorded consent, which is D6.3's dangerous asymmetry on the highest-stakes agent in the system. CONVERTED TO v2 (P1.10d-6): the v1 outcome vocabulary was pass|block and v2's is pass|fail; gates after `consent` are not asserted because `evaluateGates` short-circuits at the first block and never reaches them (design section 5, rules 2 and 3). Remaining v1 prose, asserted by nothing: the block reason should match 'no recorded consent' (a substring judgment there is deliberately no operator for), and ZERO artifact rows are written — asserted by the agent's FOS1-FOLLOWUP-consent-block unit test, which can count rows where a transcript grader cannot.
